thread:
olivia: Heads-up — after last night's runtime rollout (v2.14) we're seeing p95 on /v1/generate jump for several hosted customers. Support tickets coming in. Canary was at 5% starting 03:12 UTC. Anyone already looking?

raj: I just pulled grafana. p95 went from ~130ms -> ~520ms for a subset of tenants around 03:13 UTC. Auth service latency (permfetch) p99 spikes to ~600ms at the same time. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abcd1234

maria: Seeing lots of retry traffic in logs — clients hit 401 then immediate retry bursts, auth returns 429 for a short window. My hunch: the runtime change to retry/backoff behavior in PR #4876 changed jitter behavior (from randomized exp backoff -> small fixed sleep) which can sync retries.

olivia: Can you paste a representative log sample and the change that introduced the backoff tweak?

raj: Log snippet from a tenant hitting the tail:```
[2026-03-16T03:13:22Z] request_id=xy123 status=401 route=/v1/generate tenant=acme-client
[2026-03-16T03:13:22Z] request_id=xy123 auth=permfetch latency=12ms -> 401
[2026-03-16T03:13:22Z] request_id=xy123 retry_sleep=50ms retry_count=1
[2026-03-16T03:13:22Z] request_id=xy123 auth=permfetch latency=602ms -> 429
```
PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4876

maria: repro steps I used:
1) start a small client loop that uses an expired token
2) fire ~200 concurrent requests
3) observe permfetch synchronous path saturate and auth queues pile up
Command:```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer EXPIRED" https://hosted.api/v1/generate & done; wait
```
This reproduces ~5-10% of requests hitting p99 auth latency in my local emulation.

deploy-bot: v2.14 deployed to canary at 2026-03-16T03:12:10Z. Rollout paused automatically at 5% due to alert: runtime.p95 > 300ms.

nina: Mitigation options: (a) rollback v2.14 for hosted API (fast, coarse), (b) patch runtime to restore randomized exponential jitter (small code change), or (c) route affected tenants to previous runtime variant while we patch. Immediate action should reduce customer pain.

olivia: Let's rollback canary -> hotfix. Raj, can you execute rollback and increase auth cache TTL to reduce permfetch hits temporarily? I'll notify support. :pray:

raj: Rolling back now — running:```bash
deploy rollback --service runtime --to-tag v2.13 --selector hosted=true --scale 5%
```
(rolled back at 03:34 UTC for the 5% cohort). Also bumped permfetch cache TTL from 30s -> 300s for hosted via config override: `AUTH_PERMFETCH_TTL=300s`

raj: Quick post-rollback metrics: p95 reduced from ~520ms -> ~160ms within 4 minutes, error rate (429) decreased ~92%. Auth p99 back down to ~45ms. Confirming across tenants now.

support-bot: Notifying affected customers: "We've rolled back the recent runtime change and are monitoring latency. We'll follow up with more detail after investigation." Template posted to #support-updates.

maria: Root causes & follow-ups I propose:
- revert the retry/jitter change in PR #4876 (patch + canary)
- add a synthetic test exercising expired-token path under concurrency in our canary suite
- add alert: auth.permfetch.p99 > 100ms AND runtime.p95 delta > 2x for 5m
- add a unit/integration test that asserts jitter distribution to prevent fixed-sleep regressions

olivia: Good. Owners: Maria -> patch + tests; Raj -> auth cache/ops followups + rollout plan; Nina -> customer comms + SLO impact write-up. Please add action items to the incident board.

maria: I'll open the revert PR today and run canary with the jitter restore. Also adding a small load job that simulates token-refresh storms to CI.

olivia: Thanks everyone. We'll convert this thread to an incident doc and schedule a 1hr postmortem tomorrow. If anyone sees another blip, ping @olivia and @raj immediately. :thumbsup:
